homepage.title: Can You Pass This IQ Challenge?
homepage.summary: Try 11 quick rounds of patterns, logic, numbers, mental grids, and sharp observation.

heroPoints: Patterns, logic, mental grids, and number sense

footer.aboutText: This IQ-style challenge is a broad reasoning quiz for entertainment, self-challenge, and curiosity. It uses pattern spotting, number sense, logical thinking, mental grids, memory checks, and careful comparison. It is not a scientific IQ test, clinical assessment, school exam, job test, or official measure of intelligence.

landing.quickStartText: Starts simple. Gets sharper each round.

stageGroups.title: Quick Signal Check
stageGroups.encouragement: Good start. The first round checks fast observation and simple rules. Next, the patterns begin to layer.

questions.prompt: Which item does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Circle, square, and triangle are shapes. A spoon is an object with a different use.

questions.prompt: If you overtake the person in second place, what place are you in?
questions.explanation: If you pass the person in second place, you take their place. You are now second.

questions.prompt: Book is to reading as cup is to ____.
questions.explanation: A book is commonly used for reading, and a cup is commonly used for drinking.

questions.prompt: Imagine a row of tiles: dark, light, dark, light, ____. Which tile comes next?
questions.explanation: The row alternates dark and light, so the next tile is dark.

questions.prompt: All squares have four sides. This shape is a square. What must be true?
questions.explanation: The rule says every square has four sides.

questions.prompt: A doctor gives you 3 pills and says, "Take one now, then one every 30 minutes." How long until all pills are taken?
questions.explanation: You take the first pill now, the second after 30 minutes, and the third after 60 minutes.

questions.prompt: Which month has at least 28 days?
questions.explanation: Every month has at least 28 days.

questions.prompt: Remember this pair for later: blue - 7. What color was paired with 7?
questions.explanation: The pair given in the question was blue - 7.

stageGroups.title: Pattern Starter
stageGroups.encouragement: Nice work. This round turns simple rules into short patterns, positions, and comparisons.

questions.prompt: Which option can still be read as a number upside down?
questions.explanation: 6, 8, and 9 can each still be read as a number when turned upside down, so all of them fit.

questions.prompt: A farmer has 17 sheep. All but 9 run away. How many remain?
questions.explanation: All but 9 run away, so 9 sheep remain.

questions.prompt: A box has 5 red tokens and 2 blue tokens. How many tokens are in the box?
questions.explanation: The total is found by adding both groups together: 5 plus 2 equals 7.

questions.prompt: Imagine a 2 by 2 grid. Top left is A, top right is B, bottom left is C. What is directly below B?
questions.explanation: B is in the top-right cell, so the cell directly below it is the bottom-right cell.

questions.prompt: All lamps give light. This object is a lamp. What must be true?
questions.explanation: If all lamps give light, then this lamp gives light.

questions.prompt: What comes next: small, medium, large, small, medium, ____?
questions.explanation: The cycle is small, medium, large, then it repeats.

questions.prompt: A 2 by 2 grid has a dot in the top-left cell. After a half turn, where is the dot?
questions.explanation: A half turn moves the top-left position to the bottom-right position.

questions.prompt: Which option is the most careful answer when the facts are incomplete?
questions.explanation: May be true is careful because it does not claim more than the facts allow.

stageGroups.title: Number Moves
stageGroups.encouragement: Good focus. Now the number rules become quicker and slightly less obvious.

questions.prompt: What comes next: 3, 6, 12, 24, ____?
questions.explanation: Each number is doubled, so 24 becomes 48.

questions.prompt: Five people stand in a line. Anna stands to the left of Ben. Ben stands to the left of Cara. Which statement must be true?
choices: Cara is to the left of Anna
Anna is to the left of Cara
Ben is to the right of Cara
questions.explanation: If Anna is to the left of Ben and Ben is to the left of Cara, Anna must be to the left of Cara.

questions.prompt: A is left of B, and B is left of C. Which option cannot be correct?
choices: B is between A and C
questions.explanation: If A is left of B and B is left of C, then C cannot be left of A.

questions.prompt: What comes next: 1, 4, 9, 16, ____?
questions.explanation: These are square numbers: 1, 4, 9, 16, then 25.

questions.prompt: Imagine three boxes in a row. The first has 2 dots, the second has 4 dots, and the third has 8 dots. How many dots should the next box have?
questions.explanation: The number of dots doubles each time: 2, 4, 8, then 16.

questions.prompt: Five seats are in a row. A sits to the left of B. C sits to the right of B. Which person cannot be in the far-left seat?
questions.explanation: C is to the right of B, so C cannot be in the far-left seat.

questions.prompt: A room contains only cats and dogs. One animal is not a dog. What must it be?
questions.explanation: If the room contains only cats and dogs, an animal that is not a dog must be a cat.

questions.prompt: Which rule explains this pattern: 2, 6, 18, 54?
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 3: 2, 6, 18, then 54.

stageGroups.title: Imagine The Grid
stageGroups.encouragement: Nice reasoning. This round asks you to hold a simple grid in your head and apply the rule carefully.

questions.prompt: Imagine a 3 by 3 grid. The center cell is filled. Which cell is directly above it?
questions.explanation: The cell directly above the center is the top-middle cell.

questions.prompt: Imagine this row: circle, square, triangle, circle, square, ____. What comes next?
questions.explanation: The row repeats circle, square, triangle.

questions.prompt: Imagine a 2 by 3 grid with two rows. The top row is 1, 2, 3. The bottom row is 4, 5, 6. Which number is below 2?
questions.explanation: In the same column as 2, the number below it is 5.

questions.prompt: A mark moves right, right, down, right, right, down. What comes next?
questions.explanation: The repeating pattern is right, right, down.

questions.prompt: Imagine four tiles in a square. The top-left and bottom-right tiles are dark. What relationship do they have?
choices: They are in the same row
They are in the same column
questions.explanation: Top-left and bottom-right are diagonal from each other.

questions.prompt: A shape points up, then right, then down, then left. If the pattern continues, where does it point next?
questions.explanation: The shape turns one quarter each step and returns to up after left.

questions.prompt: Imagine a 3 by 3 grid. A mark starts in the top-left cell, moves one cell right, then one cell down. Where is it?
questions.explanation: From top-left, one right reaches top-middle, then one down reaches the center.

questions.prompt: In a 3 by 3 grid, which cell is opposite the top-left cell through the center?
questions.explanation: The cell opposite top-left through the center is bottom-right.

stageGroups.title: Memory And Focus
stageGroups.encouragement: Good attention. This round mixes small memory checks with careful reading and exact details.

questions.prompt: Earlier in the quiz, what color matched the number 7?
questions.explanation: The first round gave the pair blue - 7.

questions.prompt: Read carefully: choose the answer that says second.
questions.explanation: The instruction asks for the answer that says second.

questions.prompt: Remember this pair for later: river - square. Which shape is paired with river?
questions.explanation: The pair given in the question was river - square.

questions.prompt: A code word is planet. Which choice repeats the code word exactly?
questions.explanation: Planet exactly repeats the code word.

questions.prompt: Earlier, a color was paired with 7. Which number was paired with blue?
questions.explanation: The first memory pair was blue - 7.

questions.prompt: A list says: red, green, blue. Which color was in the middle?
questions.explanation: Green is between red and blue.

questions.prompt: Which number appears only once: 4, 8, 4, 9, 8?
questions.explanation: 9 appears once. 4 and 8 appear twice.

questions.prompt: A, B, and C stand in a line. A is before B, and B is before C. Who cannot be first?
questions.explanation: C comes after B, so C cannot be first.

stageGroups.title: Logic Links
stageGroups.encouragement: Strong progress. Now the best answer depends on what must follow, not what merely sounds possible.

questions.prompt: All clean cups are on the shelf. This cup is clean. What follows?
questions.explanation: The rule says every clean cup is on the shelf.

questions.prompt: Some books are old. All old books are rare. What can be concluded?
questions.explanation: The books that are old are also rare, so some books are rare.

questions.prompt: If no square is round, and this shape is square, what must be true?
questions.explanation: The rule says no square is round.

questions.prompt: Only verified notes are saved. A note was saved. What must be true?
questions.explanation: If only verified notes are saved, a saved note must be verified.

questions.prompt: Which statement is the safest conclusion from limited evidence?
questions.explanation: It is safer to say evidence supports one possible answer than to claim too much.

questions.prompt: A person says a plan is good because it is popular. What is the weakness?
choices: Popular does not always mean good
questions.explanation: Popularity alone does not prove that a plan is good.

questions.prompt: All approved forms are signed. Form B is approved. What follows?
questions.explanation: If every approved form is signed, an approved Form B must be signed.

questions.prompt: Which claim needs the most support?
questions.explanation: Calling something the best method is a broad claim that needs evidence.

stageGroups.title: Rule Switching
stageGroups.encouragement: You are past the easy middle. These questions reward switching rules cleanly and avoiding traps.

questions.prompt: What comes next: 2, 5, 11, 23, ____?
questions.explanation: Each term doubles and adds 1: 2, 5, 11, 23, then 47.

questions.prompt: Four people finish a race. Ben finishes before Cara. Cara finishes before Dan. Which statement must be true?
questions.explanation: The question states that Ben finishes before Cara, so that statement must be true.

questions.prompt: Which number completes the pattern: 1, 2, 6, 24, ____?
questions.explanation: The pattern multiplies by 2, then 3, then 4. Next is times 5, giving 120.

questions.prompt: Which statement is strongest?
questions.explanation: Many examples provide stronger support than one or two examples, while still avoiding a claim of absolute proof.

questions.prompt: What comes next: 4, 6, 10, 18, 34, ____?
questions.explanation: The increases are 2, 4, 8, and 16. The next increase is 32, giving 66.

questions.prompt: A statement says: "Every card that is green is numbered." This card is green. What must be true?
questions.explanation: The rule says every card that is green is numbered, and this card is green.

questions.prompt: A pattern alternates add 2, multiply by 3: 2, 4, 12, 14, ____.
questions.explanation: After 14, the rule is multiply by 3, giving 42.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion is safest?
questions.explanation: The safest conclusion is that evidence supports an idea without proving every possible case.

stageGroups.title: Spatial Reasoning
stageGroups.encouragement: Excellent. Now the visual rules use position, symmetry, and small mental movements.

questions.prompt: Imagine a 3 by 3 grid. The left column is filled. Which option describes it?
choices: Three cells in a vertical line
Three cells in a horizontal line
questions.explanation: A column runs vertically, so the left column is three cells in a vertical line.

questions.prompt: A diagram shows A left of B, B left of C, and C left of D. Which is second from the right?
questions.explanation: The order from left to right is A, B, C, D. Second from the right is C.

questions.prompt: Imagine a shape mirrored across a vertical line. What changes most directly?
questions.explanation: A vertical mirror swaps left and right positions.

questions.prompt: A mark starts at the center of a 3 by 3 grid, moves up, then right, then down. Where does it end?
questions.explanation: From center, up goes to top-middle, right goes to top-right, and down goes to middle-right.

questions.prompt: Which pattern uses symmetry?
choices: Left side matches the right side
questions.explanation: Symmetry means one side matches another side in position or shape.

questions.prompt: Imagine a row with positions 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. A mark is at 2 and moves two spaces right. Where is it?
questions.explanation: Moving two spaces right from 2 reaches 4.

questions.prompt: A 2 by 2 grid has a dot in the top-left cell. If it is rotated halfway around the center, where does the dot move?
questions.explanation: A half turn moves the top-left position to the bottom-right position.

questions.prompt: A shape turns one quarter clockwise from pointing left. Where does it point?
questions.explanation: A clockwise quarter turn from left points up.

stageGroups.title: Assumption Check
stageGroups.encouragement: Sharp work. This round asks what is hidden inside a statement or argument.

questions.prompt: Claim: The room is full, so the talk must be useful. What is assumed?
choices: Full rooms always mean useful talks
questions.explanation: The claim assumes attendance proves usefulness, which may not be true.

questions.prompt: No one complained, so everyone was happy. What is the weakness?
choices: People may be unhappy without complaining
questions.explanation: Silence does not always mean satisfaction.

questions.prompt: All complete reports include dates. This report has no date. What follows?
choices: It is not complete by that rule
questions.explanation: If complete reports need dates, a report without a date is not complete by the rule.

questions.prompt: Which statement is a counterexample to 'all boxes are light'?
questions.explanation: A heavy box challenges the rule that all boxes are light.

questions.prompt: A result improved after practice, but the questions changed. What is the concern?
choices: The new questions may be easier
questions.explanation: If the questions changed, the improvement may be due to easier questions.

questions.prompt: A conclusion depends on a missing fact. What should you do?
questions.explanation: A missing fact should be checked before relying on the conclusion.

questions.prompt: Which claim is most balanced?
choices: This result may support the idea
questions.explanation: May support the idea is balanced because it avoids overstating the result.

questions.prompt: A study uses 8 people to represent millions. What is the main concern?
choices: The sample may be too small
questions.explanation: A very small sample may not represent a much larger group.

stageGroups.title: Layered Patterns
stageGroups.encouragement: Nearly there. These questions combine more than one step, so slow down just enough to see the rule.

questions.prompt: What comes next: 5, 9, 17, 33, ____?
questions.explanation: Each number doubles and subtracts 1. 33 doubled is 66, and 66 minus 1 is 65.

questions.prompt: A hidden number is greater than 20, less than 30, and even. Which option cannot be it?
questions.explanation: 27 is odd, so it cannot match the rule that the hidden number is even.

questions.prompt: Imagine a 3 by 3 grid. The top row has 1, 2, 3. The middle row has 4, 5, 6. The bottom row has 7, 8, 9. Which number is diagonal from 1 through the center?
questions.explanation: The diagonal from 1 through the center continues to 9.

questions.prompt: Earlier, blue was paired with 7. Which option shows the exact pair?
questions.explanation: The exact pair shown earlier was blue - 7.

questions.prompt: Two answers fit the facts, but one uses fewer unsupported assumptions. Which is usually stronger?
choices: The one with fewer unsupported assumptions
The one with the longer title
questions.explanation: When two answers fit the facts, fewer unsupported assumptions usually make one stronger.

questions.prompt: A route is blocked. What is the most flexible response?
questions.explanation: Looking for another route adapts to the problem.

questions.prompt: Earlier, the exact code word was planet. Which option shows it was changed?
questions.explanation: Plant is not exactly the same as planet, so the word was changed.

questions.prompt: Earlier, which shape was paired with river?
questions.explanation: The memory pair was river - square.

questions.prompt: What comes next: 1, 2, 6, 24, 120, ____?
questions.explanation: The pattern multiplies by 2, 3, 4, and 5. Next is times 6, giving 720.

questions.prompt: Five lights are numbered 1 to 5. Light 3 is on. Light 2 is immediately left of it. Which light is immediately right of it?
questions.explanation: If Light 2 is immediately left of Light 3, then Light 4 is immediately right of Light 3.

questions.prompt: If every proven claim has evidence, which statement follows?
choices: If a claim has no evidence, it is not proven
If a claim has evidence, it is proven
questions.explanation: A claim without evidence cannot be proven by that rule.

questions.prompt: Imagine a 4-cell row: A, B, C, D. If the row is reversed, which letter becomes second?
questions.explanation: Reversing A, B, C, D gives D, C, B, A. The second letter is C.

questions.prompt: A pattern alternates multiply by 2, add 3: 4, 8, 11, 22, 25, ____.
questions.explanation: After 25, the next operation is multiply by 2, giving 50.

questions.prompt: Earlier, which color was paired with 7?
questions.explanation: The earlier memory pair was blue - 7.

questions.prompt: Five seats are in a row. Tom sits somewhere left of Mia. Mia sits somewhere left of Sam. Who must sit to the right of Mia?
questions.explanation: Mia sits somewhere left of Sam, so Sam must be to the right of Mia.

questions.prompt: Earlier, which memory pair appeared after blue - 7?
questions.explanation: Blue - 7 appeared first. River - square appeared later as another memory pair.
